problem: Train one real-world control policy from diverse language-labelled robot demonstrations and assess new-instruction, distractor, background and long-horizon generalization.
contribution: RT-1 combines language-conditioned visual tokenization, TokenLearner compression and a decoder-only transformer for efficient discrete action prediction at scale.
algorithm: Behavioral clone successful episodes. Encode6RGB frames with EfficientNet-B3 and FiLM-conditioned language embeddings; compress each image to8tokens, process48tokens through an8layer transformer and predict discretized action variables with categorical cross entropy.
observations: Six300×300RGB frames and Universal Sentence Encoder task description; model does not infer measured grip force merely from text conditioning.
actions: Seven arm/gripper variables, three planar-base variables and a discrete arm/base/terminate mode; each variable uses256uniform bins within declared bounds.
embodiment_and_data: Everyday Robots mobile manipulators with7DOF arms; over130Kepisodes and700instructions collected with13robots over17months, across classroom/office kitchen environments.
experiments: Seen/unseen instruction combinations,30distractor tasks,22background tasks, heterogeneous-data ablations and15long-horizon instructions in two kitchens via SayCan. Planning and execution success are separate metrics.
baselines: Gato, BC-Z, enlarged BC-Z and SayCan variants; dataset quantity/diversity and model-component ablations. Original SayCan uses a slightly different prompt, explicitly noted under the long-horizon table.

quantitative_result.value: Table2 reports RT-1 seen97%,unseen76%,distractor83%,background59%. These are different task sets, not four measurements of one common task; exact trial multiplicity/training-seed count not extracted here. Table6 reports planning87% and execution67% for RT-1 in each kitchen, illustrating their distinction.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p10 Table2 and p14 Table6; p9 defines evaluation sets

limitations: Imitation need not surpass demonstrators; unseen instructions recombine familiar concepts rather than establish completely new motions. Demonstrated tasks are not very dexterous. Large collection scale and fixed source morphology cannot be assumed for local low-cost arms.
code_and_license: Primary architecture/data/evaluation examined; original executable checkpoints, source license and dataset permissions were not audited in this review. No RT-1 reproduction is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Use as architecture and data-diversity context. Any local implementation must map base stop/mode semantics, bound joint/Cartesian units and measure its own timing. A generated plan is not a completed sequence; keep planning and execution outcomes separate.
